overall: The AG found the Auburn Finance Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by approving its August 4, 2021 minutes at a March 2022 meeting, far beyond the 30-day/three-meeting limit; staff shortage was no excuse. The AG ordered future compliance, declined extra allegations, and gave no further relief since the minutes were approved.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee failed to approve the minutes of its August 4, 2021 meeting in a timely manner.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to approve the minutes of the August 4, 2021, meeting in a timely manner.

allegations.summary: Additional allegations raised in the complainant's request for further review were not reviewed by the AG.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review any additional allegations made in the request for further review.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
Caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law (no further relief ordered because the minutes were already approved)
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
